title: Britain's Biggest Train Robbers Were Given Away by a Board Game

narration: Britain's biggest train robbers got away with £2.6 million.
Then a board game gave them away.
shots.visual_description: gt11 farmhouse (warm grade); gt11_robber_a (silhouette): sit -> present -> sit -> hands_together; gt11_robber_c (silhouette): sit -> arms_crossed -> present; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label '£2.6 MILLION', circle.

sources.claim_text: About £2.6 million was taken (Guinness World Records lists £2,631,784 under 'Greatest robbery from a train'), a record for a train robbery.
Summary: the record haul was given away by fingerprints on everyday things at the hideout, notably the Monopoly set and a ketchup bottle, which helped convict the gang.

narration: August 1963. The overnight mail train from Glasgow to London.
A signal turned red. It was a fake.
shots.visual_description: gt11 railway (night grade); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label '8 AUGUST 1963', callout 'A RIGGED SIGNAL'.

sources.claim_text: In the early hours of 8 August 1963 the Royal Mail's overnight travelling post office train from Glasgow to London was robbed near Cheddington, Buckinghamshire.
The gang stopped the train with a fake red signal at Sears Crossing: the green lamp was covered (a glove is named) and the red lamp powered by a battery.

narration: The train stopped. The driver, Jack Mills, was attacked and badly hurt.
shots.visual_description: gt11 railway (night grade); camera push/pull; overlays: label 'JACK MILLS'.

sources.claim_text: The driver, Jack Mills, was struck on the head and seriously hurt during the robbery. (He died in 1970; the cause is disputed and is not attributed to the attack in the episode.)

narration: At a bridge down the line, they unloaded the mailbags.
shots.visual_description: gt11 railway (night grade); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'BRIDEGO BRIDGE'.

sources.claim_text: The locomotive and front coaches were then moved on to Bridego (Railway) Bridge, where the mailbags were unloaded into waiting vehicles (on screen only).

narration: They vanished to a hideout called Leatherslade Farm.
shots.visual_description: gt11 farmhouse (night grade); gt11_robber_b (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense (walks); gt11_robber_a (silhouette): stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'LEATHERSLADE FARM'.

sources.claim_text: The gang hid at Leatherslade Farm, near Oakley, Buckinghamshire, bought weeks earlier as a hideout.

narration: There, they passed the time playing Monopoly.
Legend says they used real cash. Never proven.
shots.visual_description: gt11 farmhouse (warm grade); gt11_robber_c (silhouette): stand -> arms_crossed -> hand_to_face; gt11_robber_a (silhouette): sit -> present -> sit; gt11_robber_b (silhouette): sit -> hands_together -> point; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'LEGEND: THEY PLAYED / WITH THE REAL CASH?', stamp 'NEVER PROVEN'.

overlays.text: LEGEND: THEY PLAYED / WITH THE REAL CASH?

sources.claim_text: While hiding at the farm, the gang played Monopoly.

The story that they played with the real stolen banknotes is widely repeated (Oxford Times: 'playing with real £5 notes'; museum notices: 'reputed to have used real money') but rests on hearsay; no reputable source confirms it. Narrated as a legend, never proven.

narration: Five days later, a herdsman tipped off police.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); gt11_detective: read -> stand -> point_up; agent_a: read -> present -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '13 AUGUST 1963'.

sources.claim_text: On 13 August 1963, five days after the robbery, a local herdsman tipped off police about the farm, and officers went there.

narration: The gang had fled early.
Most of the money? Never recovered.
But they left mailbags, food... and the board game.
shots.visual_description: gt11 farmhouse (night grade); gt11_detective: stand -> examine -> stand -> point (walks); agent_a: torch -> torch_low -> torch; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label 'THE FARM WAS EMPTY', funfact 'Most of the £2.6 million / was never recovered.', circle, circle, circle.

overlays.text: Most of the £2.6 million / was never recovered.

sources.claim_text: The gang had left the farm sooner than planned, abandoning evidence: empty mailbags, shelves of food and the getaway vehicles.
FUN FACT: most of the stolen money was never recovered (Guinness World Records gives £343,448 recovered of £2,631,784).
Police lifted the gang's fingerprints from everyday objects at the Leatherslade Farm hideout, including the Monopoly board and pieces and a ketchup bottle.

narration: Then came the fingerprints.
On the Monopoly board.
And on the ketchup bottle.
shots.visual_description: gt11 farmhouse (cold grade); scientist: stand -> examine -> realise -> point; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label 'FINGERPRINT POWDER', circle, callout 'PRINTS'.

sources.claim_text: Police lifted the gang's fingerprints from everyday objects at the Leatherslade Farm hideout, including the Monopoly board and pieces and a ketchup bottle.

narration: Some belonged to Ronnie Biggs.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); analyst: examine -> stand -> arms_crossed; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: funfact 'Ronnie Biggs's prints were / on the ketchup bottle.', stamp 'MATCH'.

overlays.text: Ronnie Biggs's prints were / on the ketchup bottle.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: Ronnie Biggs's fingerprints were found at the farm, on a ketchup bottle.

narration: In 1964, the prints helped convict them. Seven got thirty years.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (sepia grade); judge: sit -> gavel -> sit; gt11_robber_a (silhouette): stand -> bowed; gt11_robber_c (silhouette): stand -> hands_together; gt11_robber_b (silhouette): stand -> hands_together; barrister: stand -> point -> hands_behind; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'APRIL 1964 · AYLESBURY / 7 MEN JAILED / FOR 30 YEARS EACH'.

overlays.text: APRIL 1964 · AYLESBURY / 7 MEN JAILED / FOR 30 YEARS EACH

sources.claim_text: Fingerprints from the farm helped convict the gang. After a trial at Aylesbury, sentences were passed in April 1964: seven men got 30 years each and five others got shorter terms.

narration: In 1965, Biggs escaped over the prison wall, on a rope ladder.
shots.visual_description: gt11 prison wall (dawn grade); gt11_biggs (silhouette): stand_tense -> stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'WANDSWORTH PRISON', funfact 'He'd served only / about 15 months of / a 30-year sentence.'.

overlays.text: He'd served only / about 15 months of / a 30-year sentence.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: on 8 July 1965, about 15 months into a 30-year sentence, Biggs escaped from Wandsworth Prison, London, going over the wall on a rope ladder into a waiting furniture van.

narration: Decades on the run. Then, in 2001, he flew home and was arrested.
shots.visual_description: press hall (cold grade); press_operator: stand -> read_newspaper -> realise -> examine; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '1965-2001 · ON THE RUN', label 'MAY 2001 · HE FLEW HOME', stamp 'ARRESTED'.

sources.claim_text: Biggs spent decades as a fugitive abroad, in Australia and then, from about 1970, in Brazil, which did not extradite him.
In May 2001, aged 71 and in poor health, he flew back to Britain voluntarily on a jet arranged by The Sun and was arrested by Scotland Yard officers on arrival.

narration: Britain's biggest train robbery, given away by a board game.

sources.claim_text: Summary: the record haul was given away by fingerprints on everyday things at the hideout, notably the Monopoly set and a ketchup bottle, which helped convict the gang.
About £2.6 million was taken (Guinness World Records lists £2,631,784 under 'Greatest robbery from a train'), a record for a train robbery.

narration: Next: how a parking ticket led police to the Son of Sam.

sources.claim_text: Next-case tease: David Berkowitz, the 'Son of Sam', was arrested on 10 August 1977 after police traced a parking ticket, issued near the last shooting in Brooklyn on 31 July 1977, to his car.
